note: Decode is weight-bandwidth-bound and the GEMMs are already efficient. One decode token at a 106-token context is 16.967 ms of kernel time over 497 dispatches, of which 187 are single-row SGEMV calls (rocblas_gemvt_warp_reduce_kernel, 74.88 us each) taking 82.5%. The text model is 2342 MB of fp32 weights, so the token streams weights at 138 GB/s aggregate and 167 GB/s inside the GEMMs alone. The ~11 ms/token floor quoted earlier was an estimate assuming ~200 GB/s achievable; measured, the gap to that estimate is ~6 ms/token, split between the 17.5% of decode that is not GEMM (GDN recurrent 10.1%, 1.71 ms) and the ~20% of bandwidth headroom left in the SGEMV calls. Transfers are not a bottleneck: 58 ms over 200 decode steps is 0.29 ms/token, 1.7% of decode. Context length is the other axis: at a 1066-token context decode is 26.737 ms/token (1.58x), driven by attention (Tensile Cijk_ kernels, 22.2%) and evie_softmax (2.5%) rather than by the projections. Vision is superlinear in patch count: 27.097 ms for 256 patches (16x16 grid) versus 1019.203 ms for 4096 patches (64x64 grid), 37.6x for 16x the patches, with gemm_library at 77.5% and evie_softmax at 12.4% on the large page. Prefill is close to linear (95.599 ms at 106 tokens, 793.623 ms at 1066). Candidate directions, in the order this profile supports: (1) cut the 187 per-token dispatches, since 497 launches per token is a launch-overhead and tail-effect cost on top of the bandwidth; (2) the GDN recurrent 10.1%; (3) attention and softmax for long contexts; (4) tiled vision attention, which the superlinear vision scaling and the separate quadratic-scratch admission cap both point at.
